Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic and work
At the end of the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme (30 September 2021) 16% of businesses reported having had employees on furlough.
Between 3 and 14 November 2021, around two-thirds (67%) of working adults in Great Britain reported travelling to work.

body.h4: Over two-thirds of working adults are travelling to work
body.h5: Percentage of working adults, Great Britain, January to November 2021
body.text: Between 3 and 14 November 2021, around two-thirds (67%) of working adults in Great Britain reported travelling to work at some point in the past seven days. 3 in 10 working adults (30%) reported working from home at some point in the past seven days.

Employment and furlough

body.h4: Almost one in six businesses reported having had employees on furlough at the end of the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme
body.text: Almost one in six businesses reported having had employees on furlough at the end of the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme

body.h4: Almost one in six businesses reported having had employees on furlough at the end of the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme
body.text: The Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme (CJRS) ended on 30 September 2021. In late October 2021, 16% of businesses not permanently stopped trading were reported to have had employees on furlough at the end of the CJRS.

body.h4: Almost one in six businesses reported having had employees on furlough at the end of the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme
body.text: Following the end of the CJRS, those 16% of businesses were asked, approximately what proportion of those furloughed employees had:

body.h4: Almost one in six businesses reported having had employees on furlough at the end of the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme
body.text: been made permanently redundant – 3%

body.h4: Almost one in six businesses reported having had employees on furlough at the end of the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme
body.text: returned to work on increased hours – 6%

body.h4: Almost one in six businesses reported having had employees on furlough at the end of the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme
body.text: returned to work on the same number of hours – 65%

body.h4: Almost one in six businesses reported having had employees on furlough at the end of the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme
body.text: returned to work on reduced hours – 16%

body.h4: Almost one in six businesses reported having had employees on furlough at the end of the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme
body.text: voluntarily left their role – 3%

body.h4: Almost one in six businesses reported having had employees on furlough at the end of the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme
body.text: other – 8%

body.h4: Almost one in six businesses reported having had employees on furlough at the end of the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme

Further information

On this page we present work data from various surveys and publications from the Office for National Statistics including the Business Insights and Conditions Survey, the Opinions and Lifestyle Survey, and Economic activity and social change in the UK, real-time indicators.

To find out more about work data from different sources visit our [more information](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/healthandsocialcare/conditionsanddiseases/articles/moreinformationondatasourcesrelatedtocoronaviruscovid19/2020-12-11#work) page.
